name: Lindy.ai
summary: An AI teammate that lives in Slack: @mention it and it works across your other tools, sits in meetings for shared context and runs jobs on a schedule.
best_for: teams that live in Slack and want one shared teammate that sits in their meetings, runs scheduled routines and drafts replies inside the tools they already use
skip_if: you want flat, predictable automation costs across a large team — Lindy charges for every seat that touches it and the credits expire each cycle, so you pay for people whether or not they used their allowance
honest_knock: Cost tracks headcount rather than output: every colleague who so much as @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a paid seat, and a seat you remove runs to the end of the cycle with no mid-cycle proration. Credits are published now, but as ranges: an everyday ask is 2-250, a big build 1,000-2,500. So a month is still an estimate. And when the shared pool runs dry there is no top-up — Lindy pauses credit-using actions until the reset, unless an admin moves the workspace to a bigger plan.

pricing.plans_source: hand-curated from the vendor's pricing page
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-02, read on their own pricing page; every amount, credit allowance and FAQ rule unchanged since 4 September) Now sold per user, and the credit allowance is published again. Plus is $29.99/mo per user (3k credits per user per month), Pro $99.99/mo per user (15k credits, 5x Plus) and Max $199.99/mo per user (35k credits, ~12x Plus). Enterprise is quote-only. Every seat's credits pool into one workspace balance, refresh each billing cycle and do not roll over; the page sizes work as 2-250 credits for an everyday ask, 250-1,000 for deep work and 1,000-2,500 for a big build. Anyone who uses Lindy takes a paid seat, including colleagues who only @mention it in Slack — those who join that way get a 7-day free trial first, direct signups are billed straight away. All four tiers connect up to 5 inboxes, and computer use, model selection and MCP support are no longer tier-gated.
